newsitem.title: USA: Georgia house votes down anti-takeover measure.
newsitem.headline: Georgia house votes down anti-takeover measure.

text.p: The Georgia State House of Representatives voted against an anti-takeover measure that would have shielded Marietta-based Healthdyne Technologies Inc on Tuesday from a hostile takeover, sending the amendment back to the Senate by a margin of more than two-to- one.

The amendment, attached to a routine House bill, was voted down 52 to 115 after nearly an hour of debate. House officials said both the bill and the amendment would go back to the Senate, where they were approved late last week.
Should the Senate insist on its position, officials said, the measure would be relegated to a conference committee.

Healthdyne Technologies is the target of an unfriendly takeover bid by Invacare, which offered $13 a share, or about $164 million, for the company. The offer was due to expire Monday, but Invacare extended the bid to April 7.
About 23 percent of Healthdyne stock has been tendered.
The lengthy amendment,added by lawmakers from Healthdyne's district, requires staggered terms for corporate board directors, a measure that would block an attempt to replace all members at once.
